comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C11-C15. Both evaluations find the evidence for non-carbapenemase resistance compelling and well-supported through genome sequencing, machine learning, and functional assays.

Perfect agreement on claims C28-C32, C58. Both evaluations support the competitive fitness assay data showing epistatic effects across imipenem gradients without questioning the methodology or conclusions.

Perfect agreement on claims C64-C67. Both evaluations support the therapeutic recommendations, though OpenEval notes these are inferences requiring clinical validation while peer reviewers accept them without challenge.

Perfect agreement on claims C68-C70. Both evaluations support the phage therapy caution regarding porin mutations, with OpenEval noting it's a logical inference and peer reviewers accepting it as following from the resistance mechanism.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C23-C26, C50. Both evaluations support the experimental evolution data showing fitness costs and instability of resistance. Peer review also includes C93 (summary claim) and identifies this as 'a major finding.'

Strong agreement on claims C4, C43-C45, C51, C75. Both evaluations support the ceftazidime selection mechanism. Peer review also includes C94 and identifies this as 'a major finding' with compelling integration of methods.

Strong agreement on claims C18-C21. Both evaluations support the structural characterization of OmpK36 deletion. Peer review also includes C22 (complementation data) as part of the compelling genetic dissection.

Partial agreement on claims C2, C27. Both evaluations support the two-loci epistatic mechanism. OpenEval also includes C22, C26 while peer review includes C57 (efflux pump exclusion). Peer reviewers found the genetic dissection 'admirable.'

Strong agreement on claims C33-C35, C41-C42. Both evaluations support the experimental evolution results showing fitness recovery and independent deletions. Peer review also includes morphological characterization claims C36, C38-C40.

Agreement on claims C46-C48. Both evaluations support the evolutionary potential experiments. OpenEval also includes C71, C73-C74 (fitness landscape data) while peer reviewers accepted the sequential selection mechanism as compelling.

Critical disagreement on claims C5, C76. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveat about clinical validation. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly stating 'the central claims are not supported' and requiring authors to 'substantially reframe the claims' or provide patient history data. Peer review also includes C71.

Agreement on claim C56. Both evaluations support the conclusion that efflux pumps do not contribute to resistance. OpenEval also includes C57 and notes direct knockout experiments would strengthen evidence; peer reviewers accepted this negative result without challenge.

Strong agreement on claims C8-C10, C54-C55. Both evaluations support the genome annotation and resistance profile characterization. Peer review also includes C6-C7, C49 (phylogenetic and assembly data) as foundational evidence.

Partial agreement on claims C6-C7, C49. Both evaluations support the phylogenetic analysis and genome assembly. OpenEval focuses on assembly quality while peer review groups this with broader genomic characterization (C8-C10, C54-C55).

Partial agreement on claims C36, C38-C40. Both evaluations support the morphological observations from experimental evolution. OpenEval also includes C37, C96-C98 (capsule and fimbriae interpretation) while peer review groups morphology with fitness recovery data (C33-C35, C41-C42).

OpenEval evaluated claims C16-C17, C95 regarding porin gene synteny conservation as SUPPORTED based on comparative genomics. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C59-C61, C63 regarding surveillance data and prevalence as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual epidemiological claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C62, C85 regarding diagnostic limitations as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these claims about current diagnostic approaches.
OpenEval evaluated extensive background claims C77-C91 as SUPPORTED based on literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual knowledge claims.
OpenEval evaluated claim C92 regarding clinical strain origin as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this contextual claim.

OpenEval evaluated claim C93 (summary of fitness cost findings) as SUPPORTED. Peer review includes C93 within their evaluation of the experimental evolution data (R3) and identifies it as 'a major finding' without separate evaluation.
OpenEval evaluated claims C52-C53 regarding taxonomic and genetic background as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluated claim C72 regarding evolutionary principles as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this theoretical framework claim.
